washing-machine:not-draining.description: The pump filter is usually behind a flap at the bottom front. Turn the machine off and drain any water first, then twist the filter out to clear it. Typical location — your machine may differ.

washing-machine:not-draining.title: Dirty water backing up — check the household waste plumbing
washing-machine:not-draining.description: If the machine pumps out but dirty water comes back into the drum, backs up the sink, or smells of drains, the problem is usually the HOUSEHOLD WASTE PLUMBING — a blocked standpipe, waste trap/U-bend, or the kitchen sink waste the drain hose feeds into — not the machine's own pump or filter. Check and clear the standpipe and waste connection. Typical layout — your installation may differ.
washing-machine:not-draining.relatedCheck: check and clear the standpipe / household waste plumbing the drain hose empties into

washing-machine:inlet-valve.title: Where the fill-hose mesh filter is
washing-machine:inlet-valve.description: A small mesh filter sits inside the fill-hose connector at the tap/valve end and catches grit. Turn the tap off, unscrew the hose and rinse the mesh. Typical layout — your machine may differ.
washing-machine:inlet-valve.relatedCheck: check the fill hose and its inlet mesh filter

washing-machine:door-lock.title: About the door lock (interlock)
washing-machine:door-lock.description: The door lock (interlock) keeps the door shut during a wash and stops the machine starting unless the door is locked. This reference shows where it sits. If the door won't open, wait 2–3 minutes after the cycle ends for the lock to release before trying again. A faulty interlock is a replacement part best fitted by a qualified engineer.
washing-machine:door-lock.relatedCheck: identify the door lock (interlock) and the safe wait-to-release step before the door will open

washing-machine:excessive-vibration.title: Check the transit bolts have been removed
washing-machine:excessive-vibration.description: Transit bolts hold the drum still for delivery and must be removed before use — a machine that bangs, walks or vibrates (especially when new or recently moved) often still has them fitted. They unscrew from the back of the machine. Typical layout — your machine may differ.
washing-machine:excessive-vibration.relatedCheck: check the transit bolts have been removed and the machine is level

washing-machine:odour.description: The rubber door seal has a fold at the bottom where water and gunge collect and go mouldy. Peel it back gently and wipe it clean. Typical layout — your machine may differ.

washing-machine:odour.title: Drain / sewer smell — check the household waste plumbing
washing-machine:odour.description: A sharp drain or sewer smell (worst near the standpipe or after draining) usually comes from the HOUSEHOLD WASTE PLUMBING, not the machine — a dry or missing U-bend/anti-siphon trap, or the drain hose pushed in too far with no air gap. Check the standpipe, waste trap and drain-hose installation. Typical layout — your installation may differ.

tumble-dryer:not-heating.title: Tumble dryer runs but doesn't heat — what to check
tumble-dryer:not-heating.description: If the drum turns but the clothes stay wet, it's usually a heating fault — and the most common cause is restricted airflow, which you can fix yourself. Clean the fluff filter and the condenser and clear the vents/ducts. Switch the dryer off and let it cool first.
tumble-dryer:not-heating.relatedCheck: clean the fluff filter and condenser and clear the vents to restore airflow before suspecting a heating part

tumble-dryer:not-emptying-condensate.title: Where the condenser and water tank are
tumble-dryer:not-emptying-condensate.description: On a condenser dryer the water container pulls out at the top and the condenser/heat exchanger sits behind a flap at the bottom front — slide it out and rinse it. Condenser/heat-pump dryers only; layout may differ.

tumble-dryer:filter-blocked.description: The fluff/lint filter sits in the door opening or just inside the rim. Lift it out and clear the fluff after every load. Typical layout — your dryer may differ.

tumble-dryer:poor-drying.title: Tumble dryer not drying properly — what to check
tumble-dryer:poor-drying.description: Poor drying is most often caused by restricted airflow. Clean the fluff filter every cycle, clean the condenser regularly and avoid overloading the drum — these are safe checks you can do yourself. Switch the dryer off and let it cool first.

oven-cooker:uneven-heating.title: About uneven oven heating
oven-cooker:uneven-heating.description: When an oven cooks unevenly or browns on one side, the parts usually involved are the fan that circulates the heat, the element, the temperature sensor and the door seal. This reference shows where they sit and the safe checks worth making. Replacing these parts is a job for a qualified engineer.

fridge-freezer:not-cooling.title: Fridge not cooling — simple checks first
fridge-freezer:not-cooling.description: Before suspecting the sealed system, check the temperature setting, that the door seal closes cleanly, that there's air space and clean condenser coils at the back, and listen for the compressor. Unplug before cleaning at the back. A sealed-system or refrigerant repair is a job for a qualified engineer. Typical layout — your model may differ.

hobs:element.title: About the hob heating parts
hobs:element.description: When a hob zone won't heat or heats unevenly, the parts involved are the heating element/zone, the temperature sensor and the control board — and on an induction hob, the pan itself must be suitable. This reference shows where they sit and the safe checks (use the right pan, keep the surface clean, try a reset). Replacing hob parts is a job for a qualified engineer.

vacuum:lost-suction.title: Poor suction — what to check first
vacuum:lost-suction.description: Lost suction is usually a full bin, a dirty filter or a blockage in the hose, tube or floor head — check and clear those before suspecting the motor. Switch off and unplug first. Typical layout — your model may differ.
vacuum:lost-suction.relatedCheck: empty the bin, clean the filters and clear any blockage

vacuum:cuts-out.title: Poor suction — what to check first
vacuum:cuts-out.description: A vacuum that pulses or cuts out after running is usually a full bin, a dirty filter or a blockage starving the airflow — check and clear those before suspecting battery, charger or motor. Switch off and unplug first. Typical layout — your model may differ.
vacuum:cuts-out.relatedCheck: empty the bin, clean the filters and clear any blockage

oven-cooker:fan-oven-element.title: About the oven heating parts
oven-cooker:fan-oven-element.description: A fan oven that runs but doesn't heat usually points to the fan-oven element — the fan proves the oven has power, but the element is what produces the heat. This reference shows where the element and the other heating parts sit, and the safe, no-dismantle checks worth making first. Fitting a new oven element is a job for a qualified engineer.
